To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we use stacked gravitational lensing data from galaxy clusters at z ≈ 0 to fit density profiles for dark matter halos; (2) the best fit to our data is provided by a phenomenological model, the Stadel profile, and by the DARKexp model of the non-singular Isothermal sphere; (3) the NFW profile, which is the most widely used model for the dark matter distribution in galaxies and clusters, provides a suboptimal fit to our data
the best-fitting dark matter density profile is the Stadel profile, and that it is followed by the Einasto, NFW, DARKexp and Hernquist profiles, in this order, as measured by the goodness-of-fit.
the Stadel profile, the generalized NFW and the Einasto profile fit the data well, and that the DARKexp profile has a good performance, too.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mass distribution in galaxy clusters and the analysis of the results in the context of the current theories and models for dark matter.
the following ques tions: (i) What is the best-fit model of the dark matter density distribution in galaxy clusters?
a comparison of different models to describe the dark matter density profiles in clusters of galaxies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no model is clearly preferred over the others, although the NFW profile with free inner slope and Stadel profile have the best performances, followed by the Einasto model.
the NFW profile is a good fit to the lensing mass profile, but the Stadel model and the DARKexp profile are slightly preferred.
the Stadel and the DARKexp profiles are preferred over other profiles, and that a single form parameter model for DARKexp is preferred over models with more parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Stadel proﬁle is the most suitable to describe the dark matter distribution of the clusters we analyzed.
the Stadel pro ﬁle is the best model for the stacked cluster mass pro ﬁle, and that the NFW pro ﬁle can be used as an alternative if one is interested in a more robust statistical inference.
, the best fit model for the stacked lensing mass profile is the Stadel model, which has a cuspy inner profile and a steeper outer slope.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lensing mass profiles of massive galaxy clusters can provide a stringent test for dark matter density profiles.
the Stadel profile is an excel lent fit to the data and that it is not necessary to invoke a non-spherical dark matter distribution to explain the observed lensing signal.
the stacked mass pro file of high-mass galaxy clusters can be used to discriminate among different models of dark matter profiles.
